title: Quant Impact — Slicewise Ablation & Anchor Prompt Audit (AWQ/GPTQ, int8/int4)
body:
Summary:

This note records an in-progress slicewise ablation and anchor-prompt audit comparing AWQ and GPTQ quantized variants across int8 and int4 regimes for onboarding candidate models (mostly LLaMA2-family v2-style checkpoints). Goal: identify which semantic slices suffer the largest quality deltas, whether those deltas are consistent across prompt anchors, and produce a prioritized mitigation plan for production rollouts.

Status snapshot:
- experiments run on 1k prompt anchors per slice, stratified by length and few-shot context.
- automated metrics: exact-match (EM), token-level perplexity delta (approx), BLEU for structure tasks, and NDCG for ranking slices.
- human spot checks (pairwise A/B with majority vote) for top 6 worst slices.
- testing infra: dedicated small cluster with fp16 baseline, AWQ-int8, AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int8, GPTQ-int4.

Why this is different from other quant reports:
- slicewise ablation uses anchor prompts (stable seed prompts we reuse) to reduce sampling variance across runs.
- we explicitly measure prompt-anchor sensitivity: for each slice, we test 10 anchor prompts and report both median and worst-anchor delta.
- emphasis on concrete rollback/mitigation knobs (soft prompts, prefix-cache bypass, model-routing) rather than just error counts.

Methodology (short):
- slices defined by functional intent and failure mode tags: math-fewstep, code-gen, instruction-following, factual, multi-hop, legal-phrasing, conversational-context-handoff, summarization-lengthy, formatting-tables.
- anchor prompt set: curated 1k prompts across slices; each anchor repeated with 3 random seeds for sampling where applicable.
- baselines: fp16 baseline metrics recorded for same anchors.
- quant setups: AWQ-int8, AWQ-int4 (default AWQ config), GPTQ-int8, GPTQ-int4 (OG post-training quantization configs used in infra).
- eval metrics: slice-level delta_EM = EM_quant - EM_fp16, delta_NDCG, delta_avg_response_length, and human preference % vs baseline.
- significance: bootstrap 1k resamples to estimate 95% CI for delta_EM per slice-anchor.

Key findings (high-level):
1) AWQ-int8 shows small median deltas across slices (median delta_EM ~ -0.6%) but certain narrow slices have outsized degradation.
2) GPTQ-int8 similar median but slightly worse worst-anchor variance on code-gen and math-fewstep.
3) int4 regimes (both AWQ and GPTQ) amplify regressions: median delta_EM ~ -3.8% with heavy tail; largest losses in multi-hop reasoning and legal-phrasing (up to -18% on worst anchors).
4) Anchor sensitivity: for some slices (code-gen formatting, table rendering) the worst-anchor delta is double the median, indicating brittle prompt patterns.
5) Human eval alignment: automated EM deltas correlate with human preference (Spearman rho 0.71) but there are outliers where shallow token errors (formatting) lead to large EM deltas but negligible user-perceived quality loss.

Detailed slice highlights (examples):
- math-fewstep: AWQ-int8 delta_EM -1.2% (CI -0.9 to -1.6), AWQ-int4 -6.9% (CI -5.8 to -8.1). GPTQ-int4 skewed worse on longer anchors. Errors are typically arithmetic slip on intermediate step tokens, leading to incorrect final numeric output. Mitigation: prioritized fallback to fp16 for anchors with numeric-critical token patterns; use runtime heuristic to detect math prompts (regex + demonstration detection).

- code-gen: formatting-preservation slice: AWQ-int8 median delta_EM -0.4% but worst-anchor -7.4% (anchors with nested code blocks). GPTQ-int4 worst-anchor -12.5%. Failure mode: bracket/indent tokenization shifts producing small formatting diffs that break compile tests. Mitigation: apply suffix-preserve scoring and prefer model variant that maximizes formatting BLEU when route triggered; add post-generation formatter + compile-checker.

- multi-hop/factual: largest human-impact regressions in int4. AWQ-int8 median -2.1% but some anchors show -15%. Hypothesis: KV-cache quant noise accumulates across hops; longer chains amplify small per-token inaccuracies. Mitigation: increase KV read precision for multi-hop contexts (config knob experimented in this run: keep KV as fp16 while rest quantized — reduced delta by ~40%).

Quant config ablation notes:
- AWQ int4 with per-channel scales + bias correction reduced median delta by ~0.8% vs naive AWQ-int4.
- GPTQ int4 with layer-wise group-folding produced lower perplexity but higher EM variance on long-context anchors.
- Hybrid: AWQ-int4 + KV fp16 (selective precision) seems the best trade for throughput vs quality for multi-hop and conversational-context-handoff.

Human spot-check summary:
- 180 pairwise comparisons across the 6 worst slices. Raters: internal annotators (3 per pair).
- agreement Fleiss kappa 0.64 (substantial).
- for formatting-heavy failures, humans preferred quant models ~20% of the time despite EM loss because errors were non-blocking. For legal-phrasing and multi-hop, humans preferred baseline >85% of time when delta_EM exceeded 6%.

Operational implications and suggested rollout policy:
1) Default: allow AWQ-int8 for all non-critical slices with monitoring.
2) Block int4 for sinks labeled high-risk (legal, multi-hop, finance) until we have hybrid-KV solution.
3) Implement per-route model routing: map slices to quant profile using simple heuristics (pattern matching) + ML classifier trained on anchor metadata.
4) Add a preflight anchor-check during canary: run 50 anchor prompts for a new quant config in the canary pool and enforce max-worst-anchor-delta threshold (suggested 5% EM for production).
5) Add auto-fallback when runtime detects prefix patterns with known sensitivity (e.g., nested code blocks, step-by-step math).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need larger-scale human eval for legal-phrasing to quantify business risk for regulatory customers.
- Explore automated metric that better captures perceived quality for formatting tasks (validation by downstream compile/run).
- Tune AWQ per-channel calibration in the compiler to see whether we can reclaim int4 headroom without hybrid-KV.
- Instrument more production-like prompt noise (typos, paraphrase) to measure robustness.
- Build small classifier to route to fp16/hybrid-int4 at request time; prototype in runtime branch PR#784.

Appendix: quick experiment log (short)
- 2025-10-20: baseline collection (fp16) on 10k anchors.
- 2025-11-02: AWQ-int8/int4 pass v1 (default).
- 2025-11-12: GPTQ-int8/int4 pass v1.
- 2025-12-05: AWQ-int4 per-channel scale patch.
- 2026-01-18: Hybrid-KV experiment (AWQ-int4 with KV fp16).
- 2026-02-10: human spot-checks executed.

Quick links and artifacts:
- linear: RDOC-1125 (quant rollout safety thresholds)
- runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/784 (routing + preflight hooks)
- confluence page: ml/quant-standards (guidelines for quant configs)

Notes to self (raw):
- double-check statistical test code: bootstrap seed 42 used but sampling stratification might be off for very small slices (<40 anchors).
- consider moving anchor set to a small deterministic subset for canary checks (reduce noise).
- run targeted fuzz of tokens that are known to be sensitive to group quantization (e.g., long table separators).

If folks agree, next steps: convert to a short product-facing one-pager with rollout policy + suggested guardrails (SLA/thresholds) and queue infra work for per-route routing classifier.

-- Maya T.
